metadata.name: greekbet
metadata.description: GreekBet — binary YES/NO prediction markets priced by an LMSR AMM

instructions.name: buy_shares
docs: Buy `outcome` shares by depositing exactly `usdc_amount` of collateral.
Slippage is enforced **on-chain** (plan §2.3) as a floor on what the
caller receives: the trade reverts with `SlippageExceeded` unless it
credits at least `min_shares_out` share base units. `0` disables the
check but still cannot produce a zero-output trade — that is
`ZeroCostTrade`.
The plan called this argument `max_slippage`. It is named for what it
actually is: a price-based limit would have to say *which* price
(marginal-before, marginal-after, or average-paid), and those differ by
exactly the trade impact being guarded against. A minimum-output limit
needs no such choice, no second LMSR call, and no rounding decision that
could favour the caller — the worst effective price is simply
`usdc_amount / min_shares_out`, computable client-side with no knowledge
of the curve.

accounts.name: buyer
docs: The buyer. Signs the collateral transfer and pays rent the first time
they trade in this market (`init_if_needed` on `position`), hence `mut`.

accounts.name: market
docs: The market being traded. `mut` because `q_yes` / `q_no` move.
The seeds constraint mirrors `close_market`: it re-derives the market
from the `creator` and `question_hash` it stores, using the stored bump,
so this is a `create_program_address` check rather than a search.

accounts.name: position
docs: The buyer's position in this market, created on first purchase.
# Why `has_one` is absent and the seeds are the whole check
`init_if_needed` runs the account's other constraints *after* a fresh
account has been zero-initialised, so `has_one = market` would fail on
the very first buy (`Pubkey::default() != market.key()`). The seeds
constraint is strictly stronger anyway: it derives the address from
`market.key()` and `buyer.key()`, so no other account can be passed here
at all, whether it exists yet or not. The handler then (re-)writes
`market`, `owner` and `bump` unconditionally, which is idempotent for an
existing position and initialisation for a new one.

accounts.name: vault
docs: The market's collateral vault — the destination of the deposit. Pinned
to the pubkey the market stored at creation.

accounts.name: buyer_token_account
docs: Where the collateral comes from. Validated against the market's own
`collateral_mint` (D3) and required to belong to the signer, so a buyer
cannot spend a third party's account even if that account has delegated
authority elsewhere.

instructions.name: close_market
docs: Mark a market closed once `close_time` has passed. Permissionless.
**Owned by T06.**

accounts.name: market
docs: The market to close. Must currently be `Open` and past its `close_time`.

instructions.name: create_market
docs: Create a market and seed its vault with the LMSR max subsidy.
`resolver` is stored verbatim and otherwise unused in this phase.
**Owned by T06.**

accounts.name: creator
docs: Pays rent for both new accounts and funds the vault seed.

accounts.name: market
docs: The new market. Seeds are `[MARKET_SEED, creator, sha256(question)]`, so
one creator can run many markets and two creators asking the same
question cannot collide.
# Why the hash seed is written `&question_hash(&question)`
Not stylistic — the alternative does not build. Anchor 1.2.0's IDL
generator (`anchor_syn::idl::accounts::parse_seed`) can only describe
seeds that are constants, whole instruction arguments, or account
fields. A `MethodCall` seed such as `question_hash(&question).as_ref()`
falls into its catch-all branch, which re-emits the expression verbatim
into a generated function where the instruction arguments are **not** in
scope: `anchor build` then fails the IDL step with
`E0425: cannot find value 'question' in this scope`, even though the
`.so` itself compiles.
Written as a reference to a call with arguments, `parse_seed` instead
returns `Err`, `get_pda` swallows it, and the account is emitted with no
`pda` metadata — which is the correct outcome anyway, since "SHA-256 of
an argument" is not expressible in the IDL's seed vocabulary. The
on-chain derivation is unaffected: that constraint is expanded inside
`try_accounts`, where `question` is in scope.
Consequence for clients (T09/T10): `anchor.web3` cannot auto-derive this
PDA. Derive it explicitly as
`findProgramAddressSync([Buffer.from("market"), creator.toBuffer(), sha256(question)], programId)`.

accounts.name: collateral_mint
docs: The market's collateral mint — **per-market runtime config** (D3), never
a program constant.
The decimals check is what lets T08 redeem winning shares 1:1: share
counts and collateral must be the same 6-decimal base unit, and a mint
with different decimals would silently break that mapping.

accounts.name: vault
docs: The market's collateral vault: an SPL token account for
`collateral_mint` whose **authority is the market PDA** (plan §2.1), so
only this program can move collateral out of it.
Declared after `market` and `collateral_mint` because its seeds and its
`token::*` constraints reference both — Anchor resolves accounts in
declaration order.

accounts.name: creator_token_account
docs: Where the `b·ln 2` seed deposit comes from. Must hold the market's
collateral mint and belong to the creator.

instructions.name: redeem
docs: Redeem a resolved position: winning shares 1:1, losing shares zero.
**Owned by T08.**

accounts.name: owner
docs: The position holder. Must sign, and is the only key that can redeem
this position (`has_one = owner` below). Also the rent recipient when
the position account is closed, hence `mut`.

accounts.name: market
docs: The resolved market. Read-only — redemption does not move `q_yes` /
`q_no`; the LMSR state is frozen once the market resolves.
This account also supplies the seeds that sign the vault withdrawal, so
it must be a real, program-owned `Market` (which `Account<_, Market>`
enforces via owner + discriminator) sitting at its own canonical PDA
(which the `seeds`/`bump` constraint enforces).
The seeds constraint is defence in depth rather than a fix: a
non-canonical `Market` was already unusable here, because the position
PDA is derived from `market.key()`, the vault is pinned by
`address = market.vault`, and the signer derived from a forged market
would not be the vault's authority, so the CPI would fail. T09 observed
that this instruction was the only one of the six without the
constraint — safe incidentally rather than by construction. Made
explicit so the guarantee does not depend on that reasoning surviving a
future edit.

accounts.name: position
docs: The caller's position in this market.
`close = owner` returns the rent once redemption succeeds. Anchor runs
the close in `exit()`, i.e. *after* the handler body and after the token
CPI, so it cannot be used to skip the state update — the zeroing in the
handler still happens first.

accounts.name: vault
docs: The market's collateral vault. Pinned to the pubkey the market stored
at creation, so a look-alike token account cannot be substituted.

accounts.name: owner_token_account
docs: Where the payout lands. Validated against the market's own
`collateral_mint` (D3), never against a hardcoded mint.

instructions.name: resolve_market
docs: Write the winning outcome. Callable only by the stored resolver.
An access-controlled state write and nothing more — no dispute, vote, or
oracle logic in this phase. **Owned by T06.**

accounts.name: market
docs: The market to resolve. Must currently be `Closed`.

accounts.name: resolver
docs: The key stored in `market.resolver` at creation. A bare pubkey with no
logic attached (plan §2.2) — being this key and signing is the entire
authorization model.

instructions.name: sell_shares
docs: Sell `share_amount` of `outcome` back to the market.
Mirror of [`buy_shares`]: reverts with `SlippageExceeded` unless
proceeds are at least `min_usdc_out`. **Owned by T07.**

accounts.name: seller
docs: The position holder. Must sign; only this key can unwind this position.

accounts.name: market
docs: The market being traded. `mut` because `q_yes` / `q_no` move.
This account also supplies the seeds that sign the vault withdrawal, so
it is pinned to its own canonical PDA as well as being checked for owner
and discriminator by `Account<_, Market>`.

accounts.name: position
docs: The seller's position in this market.
Deliberately **not** closed when it empties out. A seller who unwinds
their whole holding keeps a zeroed position account (and its rent) and
can buy back into the same PDA without re-paying for it; `redeem` is what
finally closes it and returns the rent. Closing here would also mean an
`init_if_needed` on the buy side racing an account close in the same
slot, which is a failure mode with no upside.
The owner check is spelled out rather than written `has_one = owner`
because the signer field is `seller`, not `owner`; `has_one` matches on
the *field name* in this struct.

accounts.name: vault
docs: The market's collateral vault — the source of the payout. Pinned to the
pubkey the market stored at creation, so a look-alike token account
cannot be substituted.

accounts.name: seller_token_account
docs: Where the proceeds land. Validated against the market's own
`collateral_mint` (D3), never against a hardcoded mint.

errors.name: CloseTimeNotReached
errors.msg: Close time has not been reached

errors.name: CloseTimeInPast
errors.msg: Close time is in the past

errors.name: Unauthorized
errors.msg: Signer is not the resolver authority

errors.name: BOutOfRange
errors.msg: Liquidity parameter b is out of range

errors.name: QOutOfRange
errors.msg: Share quantity is out of range

errors.name: ZeroCostTrade
errors.msg: Trade moves zero collateral or zero shares

errors.name: InvalidMint
errors.msg: Token account mint does not match the market collateral mint

errors.name: InvalidVault
errors.msg: Vault account does not match the market vault

errors.name: VaultInsolvent
errors.msg: Vault is insolvent for this withdrawal

types.name: Market
docs: A single binary YES/NO market (plan §2.1). PDA, seeds
`[MARKET_SEED, creator, question_hash]`.
All quantities (`b`, `q_yes`, `q_no`) are 6-decimal base units — the same
unit the LMSR crate takes and returns, so they are passed straight through
with no scaling of any kind. See `docs/DESIGN_DECISIONS.md` D1.

fields.name: creator
docs: Who called `create_market` and seeded the vault.

fields.name: resolver
docs: The only key allowed to call `resolve_market`.
**A bare pubkey and nothing more** (plan §2.2/§2.3). This is an
intentional seam for a future oracle/dispute system; do not build
resolver logic against it in this phase.

fields.name: collateral_mint
docs: The SPL mint this market takes collateral in — **per market, never a
program constant** (D3). Every token account in every instruction is
validated against this.

fields.name: vault
docs: The market's collateral vault: an SPL token account for
[`Self::collateral_mint`] whose authority is this market PDA.

fields.name: question_hash
docs: SHA-256 of the question bytes. Part of the market PDA's seeds, so it is
stored rather than recomputed, and lets a client verify the stored
string was not tampered with.

fields.name: question
docs: The human-readable question, capped at
[`MAX_QUESTION_LEN`](crate::constants::MAX_QUESTION_LEN) bytes.
The cap is what makes this account fixed-size; `create_market` must
enforce it via [`validate_question_len`].

fields.name: created_at
docs: Unix timestamp of creation, from `Clock`.

fields.name: close_time
docs: Unix timestamp after which trading stops and `close_market` may be
cranked.

fields.name: b
docs: LMSR liquidity parameter, in collateral base units. Constrained to
`[lmsr::B_MIN, lmsr::B_MAX]` at creation (D4).

fields.name: q_yes
docs: Outstanding YES shares, base units. Capped at `lmsr::MAX_Q` on every buy.

fields.name: q_no
docs: Outstanding NO shares, base units. Capped at `lmsr::MAX_Q` on every buy.

fields.name: status
docs: Lifecycle state.

fields.name: winning_outcome
docs: `None` until `resolve_market` runs; `Some(_)` exactly when
[`Self::status`] is [`MarketStatus::Resolved`].
T08 must not `unwrap` this — a `None` here with a `Resolved` status is
an invariant violation and should surface as an error.

fields.name: bump
docs: Bump for the market PDA itself.

fields.name: vault_bump
docs: Bump for the vault PDA. Stored so T07/T08 can sign vault withdrawals
without re-deriving.

types.name: MarketClosed
docs: Emitted once per successful `close_market`.

fields.name: market
docs: The market that transitioned to `Closed`.

fields.name: close_time
docs: The `close_time` the market was created with.

fields.name: closed_at
docs: `Clock::unix_timestamp` when the crank actually landed. Always
`>= close_time`, and the gap is however long it took someone to crank.

fields.name: q_yes
docs: LMSR state frozen at close, so an indexer does not have to re-read the
account to know the final supply.

fields.name: q_no
docs: See [`Self::q_yes`].

types.name: MarketCreated
docs: Emitted once per successful `create_market`.

fields.name: market
docs: The new market PDA.

fields.name: creator
docs: Who created it and paid the seed.

fields.name: resolver
docs: Stored verbatim; unused in this phase.

fields.name: collateral_mint
docs: The market's collateral mint (D3).

fields.name: vault
docs: The market's collateral vault token account.

fields.name: question_hash
docs: SHA-256 of the question bytes — the third market PDA seed.

fields.name: b
docs: LMSR liquidity parameter, base units.

fields.name: seed_amount
docs: `lmsr::cost(0, 0, b)`, the amount actually moved into the vault.

fields.name: created_at
docs: `Clock::unix_timestamp` at creation.

fields.name: close_time
docs: When trading stops and `close_market` may be cranked.

types.name: MarketResolved
docs: Emitted once per successful `resolve_market`.

fields.name: market
docs: The market that transitioned to `Resolved`.

fields.name: resolver
docs: The key that resolved it — equal to `market.resolver` by construction,
emitted so an indexer need not join against the market account.

fields.name: winning_outcome
docs: The side that won. Winning shares redeem 1:1 (T08).

fields.name: resolved_at
docs: `Clock::unix_timestamp` when resolution landed.

fields.name: q_yes
docs: Final LMSR state, frozen at resolution.

fields.name: q_no
docs: See [`Self::q_yes`].

types.name: MarketStatus
docs: Lifecycle of a market. Every instruction validates it (plan §2.3).
The only legal transitions are `Open → Closed → Resolved`. Nothing moves a
market backwards.

types.name: Outcome
docs: Which side of the binary market a share or a trade refers to.
This is the program's own type, not `lmsr::Outcome`: the LMSR crate is
`no_std` and Anchor-free by design, so it cannot derive Anchor's
serialisation traits. The two are converted at the boundary with the
`From` impls below.

types.name: Redeemed
docs: Emitted on every successful redemption, including a zero-payout one.
`winning_shares` and `losing_shares` are the pre-clear snapshot, so an
indexer can reconstruct what the holder had without reading an account that
no longer exists.

fields.name: market
docs: The market that was redeemed against.

fields.name: owner
docs: The position holder and rent recipient.

fields.name: winning_outcome
docs: The side that won, per `resolve_market`.

fields.name: winning_shares
docs: Winning-side shares held immediately before the position was cleared.

fields.name: losing_shares
docs: Losing-side shares held immediately before the position was cleared.
These paid nothing.

fields.name: payout
docs: Collateral base units transferred out of the vault. Equals
`winning_shares` (1:1) and is `0` for a pure loser.

fields.name: position_closed
docs: Always `true` in this version — the `UserPosition` PDA is closed and its
rent returned to `owner`. Emitted explicitly so an indexer does not have
to infer it from program version.

types.name: SharesBought
docs: Emitted on every successful `buy_shares`.
Carries the full pre- and post-trade LMSR state so an indexer can reprice the
market at any point in its history without replaying account snapshots, and
both a marginal and an effective price so the trade's impact is visible
directly.

fields.name: market
docs: The market traded against.

fields.name: buyer
docs: Who bought, and who owns the credited position.

fields.name: outcome
docs: Which side was bought.

fields.name: collateral_in
docs: Collateral base units moved into the vault. **Exactly the
`usdc_amount` argument** — this instruction never re-prices the quote.

fields.name: shares_out
docs: Share base units credited, from [`lmsr::shares_for_cost`] (floored).

fields.name: avg_price_paid
docs: `collateral_in · UNIT / shares_out`, floored — the effective price paid
per share, on the same scale as [`Self::price_yes_after`].

fields.name: q_yes_before
docs: `market.q_yes` immediately before the trade.

fields.name: q_no_before
docs: `market.q_no` immediately before the trade.

fields.name: q_yes_after
docs: `market.q_yes` immediately after the trade.

fields.name: q_no_after
docs: `market.q_no` immediately after the trade.

fields.name: price_yes_after
docs: Marginal YES price after the trade, `UNIT`-scaled (`500_000` == `0.5`).
The NO price is `UNIT − price_yes_after`, exactly.

fields.name: position_yes_shares
docs: The buyer's YES holding after the trade.

fields.name: position_no_shares
docs: The buyer's NO holding after the trade.

types.name: SharesSold
docs: Emitted on every successful `sell_shares`.
The exact mirror of
[`SharesBought`](super::buy_shares::SharesBought), so an indexer can treat
the two as one stream of state transitions.

fields.name: market
docs: The market traded against.

fields.name: seller
docs: Who sold, and whose position was debited.

fields.name: outcome
docs: Which side was sold.

fields.name: shares_in
docs: Share base units burned from the position and removed from `q`.

fields.name: collateral_out
docs: Collateral base units moved out of the vault, from
[`lmsr::sell_return`] (floored).

fields.name: avg_price_received
docs: `collateral_out · UNIT / shares_in`, floored — the effective price
received per share, on the same scale as [`Self::price_yes_after`].

fields.name: q_yes_before
docs: `market.q_yes` immediately before the trade.

fields.name: q_no_before
docs: `market.q_no` immediately before the trade.

fields.name: q_yes_after
docs: `market.q_yes` immediately after the trade.

fields.name: q_no_after
docs: `market.q_no` immediately after the trade.

fields.name: price_yes_after
docs: Marginal YES price after the trade, `UNIT`-scaled. The NO price is
`UNIT − price_yes_after`, exactly.

fields.name: position_yes_shares
docs: The seller's YES holding after the trade.

fields.name: position_no_shares
docs: The seller's NO holding after the trade.

types.name: UserPosition
docs: One user's holdings in one market (plan §2.1, D2). PDA, seeds
`[POSITION_SEED, market, owner]`.
**Internal accounting only.** There are no SPL outcome mints, so these
shares are not transferable and not composable with other programs. That is
a deliberate, frozen decision (D2); the migration path, if it is ever
wanted, is to mint SPL tokens against the same `q_yes`/`q_no` accounting
without touching the LMSR core.
Share counts are 6-decimal base units, the same unit as collateral — which
is what makes T08's winning-share redemption a straight 1:1 mapping.

fields.name: market
docs: The market this position belongs to.

fields.name: owner
docs: The owner. Only this key may sell or redeem.

fields.name: yes_shares
docs: YES shares held, base units.

fields.name: no_shares
docs: NO shares held, base units.

fields.name: bump
docs: Bump for this PDA.

constants.name: MARKET_SEED
docs: Seed prefix for the [`Market`](crate::state::Market) PDA.
Full seeds: `[MARKET_SEED, creator.key(), question_hash]`.
Including the creator and the question hash lets the same creator run many
markets and keeps two creators asking the same question from colliding.

constants.name: POSITION_SEED
docs: Seed prefix for a [`UserPosition`](crate::state::UserPosition) PDA.
Full seeds: `[POSITION_SEED, market.key(), owner.key()]` — one position
account per (market, user) pair, per `docs/DESIGN_DECISIONS.md` D2.

constants.name: VAULT_SEED
docs: Seed prefix for the market's collateral vault (an SPL token account owned
by the market PDA).
Full seeds: `[VAULT_SEED, market.key()]`.
